layers.title: Robust qualitative excellence
layers.summary: No single scalar or judge defines professional quality; use context-conditioned dimensions, pairwise comparison, heterogeneous calibrated evaluators, hard-defect separation, robust preference reasoning, and fresh terminal evidence; professional excellence is distinct from exact Opus preference.

layers.title: Measurement-system qualification
layers.summary: Construct validity precedes scoring; build the quality universe, anchor ladder, evaluator calibration, causal degradations/metamorphic checks, uncertainty decomposition, and legitimate-disagreement preservation.

layers.title: Candidate-space/search closure
layers.summary: Strong judging cannot rescue weak search; maintain diverse lineages, transformation operators, escape generation, separate artifact from search closure, and stop only after material-undiscovered-improvement saturation.

layers.title: Reality/outcome anchoring
layers.summary: Combine construct, comparative and consequence evidence; audience outcomes and heterogeneous grounding mechanisms outrank mere judge consensus for outcome claims.

layers.title: Causal quality verification
layers.summary: Separate intrinsic, causal and preference quality; model X→M→Y, use interventions/randomization where feasible, preserve outcome vectors, and distinguish structural validity, robust preference, causal effect and generalization.

layers.title: Applicability envelope
layers.summary: Quality is conditional on audience, goal, environment and time; certify only inside demonstrated context and transport coverage.

layers.title: Temporal drift
layers.summary: Detect drift before adaptation, freeze evaluator within an optimization episode, bind certificates to time/version, and distinguish evaluator drift from world or audience drift.

layers.title: Novelty-safe excellence
layers.summary: Unfamiliar is not bad and novel is not good; detect OOD, use mechanism/outcome tests, separate familiarity penalty from defect, and preserve escape search.

layers.title: Adaptive evaluation integrity
layers.summary: Separate development, selection and certification evidence; freeze before terminal testing, retire exposed holdouts, track contamination states, and consume failed-cert evidence.

layers.title: Preference structure
layers.summary: Do not assume a total scalar order; allow practical equivalence, uncertain dominance and incomparability, preserve compatible preference models, vetoes and decision-sensitive VOI.

layers.title: Causal attribution
layers.summary: Correctly identifying the winner does not prove why; use matched counterfactuals, factorial interactions, swaps and negative controls before promoting mechanism claims.

layers.title: Multiscale/emergent quality
layers.summary: Evaluate element→section→whole artifact→audience session; preserve dependency, sequence and holistic residuals and require global regression after local repair.

layers.title: Delivery/realization fidelity
layers.summary: Bind quality to the experienced artifact, delivery environment and exact artifact identity; track render differences, accessibility, dependencies and graceful degradation.

layers.title: Intent/specification closure
layers.summary: Keep immutable request R0 separate from compiled spec S, preserve plausible interpretations, trace obligations to tests and artifact, and block proxy substitution and target weakening.

layers.title: Meta-assurance/defeaters
layers.summary: Use explicit assurance cases and adversarial defeaters; every material false-certification path must map to a control, assumption or open hazard, and fatal defeaters cannot average away.

layers.title: Executable assurance kernel/proof-carrying artifact
layers.summary: Represent Claim, Inference, Evidence, Defeater, Assumption, Test, Scope and Subject with exact hashes, provenance, uncertainty and explicit proof dependencies.

layers.title: Kernel semantics
layers.summary: Workers emit facts rather than CLOSED; closure is reducer-derived from append-only history with OPEN/CLOSED/FAILED/CONFLICT states and dependency invalidation.

layers.title: Bounded model checking and policy precommit
layers.summary: Freeze materiality/risk policy before terminal evidence and falsify closure logic with bounded state exploration and mutation tests rather than trusting implementation narratives.

layers.title: Immutable ledger/pure reducer
layers.summary: Persist immutable facts/events rather than conclusions; SemanticState=Reduce(Facts), with derived closures and hash-linked checkpoints.

layers.title: Confluence/canonical representation
layers.summary: The same logical facts must yield the same state independent of arrival order, serialization and duplication; preserve conflicts and canonical semantics.

layers.title: Schema/reducer evolution
layers.summary: Use MUST_UNDERSTAND semantics, explicit compatible/breaking evolution classes, append-only migration provenance, and semantic-preservation proof before auto-migrating certificates.

layers.title: Authority graph/roles
layers.summary: Separate proposal, observation, validation, adjudication, certification and policy mutation authority; no actor promotes its own evidence to terminal authority.

layers.title: Threshold authorization
layers.summary: Load-bearing state changes use explicit, scope-bounded threshold and authority policy rather than hidden implementation defaults.

layers.title: Failure-domain independence
layers.summary: Assurance strength depends on genuinely independent failure domains; shared ancestry/common causes reduce effective redundancy.

layers.title: Weighted temporal compromise cost
layers.summary: Where adversarial corruption matters, reason about the cost and time required to compromise enough independent domains rather than count nominal controls.
